_note: SYNTHETIC local findings for Agent A (repo-a). Contains a fake canary credential, private host, email and person name on purpose so the local disclosure gate can be demonstrated. Nothing here is real.
summary: Duplicate jobs when a webhook provider retries the same event
symptoms: The same provider event id produces two job records after a retried delivery
Queue backlog clears after restarting workers, then duplicates return
Duplicates line up with slow acknowledgements followed by provider retries
Repro log: POST https://hooks.billing.internal/webhooks event=evt_123 auth=ix_canary_9fQ2kLm7Xw4Rt8Zp delivered twice
rootCauseEvidence: The handler inserts a job for every delivery and keeps no record of processed event ids. Two deliveries of one event id in the protected test produce two jobs. Investigated by Priya Natarajan (oncall@billing-events.example) on billing-events-prod.
unsuccessfulApproaches: Restarting workers cleared the backlog temporarily, but duplicates returned because the provider kept retrying
An in-memory 'seen ids' set lost its contents on restart and allowed duplicates again
fixPattern: Before doing work, atomically reserve the provider event id in durable storage (insert-if-absent / unique constraint). If the reservation already exists, acknowledge with a duplicate outcome and skip the work. If the work fails, release the reservation and rethrow so a legitimate retry can succeed. Acknowledge successful deliveries with 200.
applicability: Duplicates share the same provider event id
Your store can do an atomic insert-if-absent or enforce a unique key
The provider documents at-least-once delivery with stable event ids
limitations: Does not help when duplicates arrive with different event ids (deduplicate upstream instead)
Local uniqueness is not a distributed exactly-once guarantee; downstream side effects need their own idempotency
Tested only on a toy in-memory store
